summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would require imported food to carry a prescribed warning about Australian health and hygiene standards and possible harm to consumers from the food.
It would create separate labelling offences for packaged imports and retail displays of unpackaged or minimally packaged food, each carrying a penalty of $500,000.
The warning requirements and related offences would start six months after royal assent, while the other provisions would start the day after royal assent.
changes: Imported packaged food would have to carry the prescribed warning when brought into Australia.
Retailers could place warnings on unpackaged items or display them prominently beside the food.
For minimally packaged food, warnings could appear on individual items, retail units or adjacent displays.
The minister could prescribe label size and other display requirements.
summary.affected: Food importers, operators of regulated retail food businesses and consumers buying imported food are affected.

speeches.speaker: Bob Katter
speeches.brief: Moved that the Imported Food Warning Labels Bill 2015 be read a second time, arguing that imported food risks, uneven inspection requirements and overseas production standards had harmed Australian producers and contributed to the decline of domestic prawn and fish farming.
